ui.wiki_intro: LiquidCat downloads video and audio from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Twitch and hundreds of other sites (via yt-dlp), and converts them with ffmpeg using GPU acceleration when available. All wrapped in a lightweight liquid-glass interface. Below is what each part of the app does.
ui.wiki_p_formats: Lists show clear options (resolution, size and container) and the best quality is marked with a star. The lists open with a smooth animation.
ui.wiki_p_output: Output type: video or audio only. Video/audio format: the specific track to download. Processing mode: Re-encode (reconverts with your settings) or Download as-is (faster, no conversion).
ui.wiki_p_encode: Hardware acceleration: NVIDIA, AMD or CPU only. Video codec: H.264, HEVC, AV1 or VP9. Audio codec: MP3, AAC, Opus, etc. Quality (CQ/CRF): lower value = better quality and larger size.
ui.wiki_p_advanced: Trim (start/end), subtitles (download or embed), metadata (title, artist and description) and cover art in MP3/M4A/FLAC (WAV metadata only), and browser cookies for restricted content (verified when picked).
ui.wiki_p_dest: Folder where the result is saved. The Browse… button opens the Windows file explorer. If you pick nothing, your Downloads folder is used.
ui.wiki_p_local: Process files on your computer without downloading anything: re-encode the video, convert to audio (MP3, AAC, Opus, FLAC…) or export a GIF with adjustable FPS and width. You can pick or drag several files at once; each one is processed in the queue.
ui.wiki_p_queue: Add several jobs to the queue, download a playlist, or use “Batch import” to paste many links at once; they are processed in order. The Cancel button stops the current download and the whole queue.
ui.wiki_p_activity: Progress bar and a friendly log in real time (technical noise is hidden and clear messages are shown: downloading, merging, saving…).
ui.wiki_p_history: Keeps your generated files with their thumbnail and info (title, channel and duration). Open each file, jump to its folder, or clear the history (with confirmation).
ui.wiki_p_settings: Switch between 14 themes (Catppuccin, Dracula, AMOLED, Dark, Light, Fluent, Gruvbox, Nord, Tokyo Night and Neo Brutalist), each with its own icon; update yt-dlp to the latest (nightly) and ffmpeg with one click, and pick the download folder. The top bar shows the status of yt-dlp, ffmpeg and the GPU (green NVIDIA, red AMD, blue CPU).
ui.wiki_p_lang: Language selector in Settings (Spanish, English, Portuguese, French, German and Italian), and Credits with the developers, the software used and the theme authors.
ui.batch_hint: Paste one link per line. They will be added to the queue with the current settings.
ui.credit_slint_desc: Native Rust UI toolkit that draws the app.
ui.wiki_p_presets: Save your settings as a preset and apply them in one click. Included: Original (max quality, no conversion), H.264 compatible (best H.264 + AAC without re-encoding, plays on any device), 1080p H.264 with subtitles, light 720p in HEVC, MP3 320 music, M4A audio without re-encoding, lossless FLAC and podcast/voice.
